breakfast.name: Fried Plantains with Pepper Sauce
ingredients: Pepper sauce: scotch bonnet, onion, tomato
instructions: Slice and fry plantains
Blend pepper sauce
Serve plantains with sauce
breakfast.description: Fried plantains with fiery pepper sauce.

breakfast.name: Pap (Fermented Corn Porridge)
instructions: Mix batter with water
Cook until thick
Sweeten

breakfast.name: Rice Porridge (Pap)
instructions: Rice porridge is the Sierra Leonean breakfast staple
The rice is ground or cooked whole until soft
Sweetened with sugar and condensed milk
A filling, affordable breakfast across Sierra Leone
breakfast.description: Sierra Leonean rice porridge -- rice ground or cooked whole until soft and porridge-thick, sweetened with sugar and condensed milk. The filling, affordable breakfast eaten across the country.

breakfast.name: Bread and Fried Egg
instructions: Fried egg on bread is the everyday Sierra Leonean breakfast
Local white bread -- slightly sweet, soft
The egg fried in a little oil
Sometimes a small chilli is fried alongside
Simple, quick, and filling
breakfast.description: Sierra Leonean everyday breakfast -- fried egg on local white bread (slightly sweet, soft). Fried in oil, often with a small chilli alongside. Simple and filling.

lunch.name: Cassava Leaf Stew
instructions: Boil pounded cassava leaves 30 min
Add palm oil, meat, fish
Simmer until thick
Serve with rice
lunch.description: The national dish of Sierra Leone.

lunch.name: Groundnut Soup
instructions: Brown chicken
Sauté vegetables
Add peanut paste and water
Simmer 30 min

lunch.name: Jollof Rice
instructions: Jollof rice is the West African party rice -- and Sierra Leone has its version
The tomato-based rice: the rice cooks in the tomato sauce
The smoky bottom (party jollof): the slightly burnt bottom layer is the prize
Cooked over wood fire for the best smokiness
The competition: Nigeria vs Ghana vs Senegal for the original -- Sierra Leone has its say
lunch.description: Sierra Leonean jollof rice -- long-grain rice cooked in a tomato-onion sauce with Scotch bonnet and spices until the liquid is absorbed. The slightly burnt bottom layer (the smoky party jollof) is the prize. Sierra Leone joins the West African jollof debate.

lunch.name: Fish and Cassava Leaf Stew
instructions: Cassava leaf stew with smoked fish is a Sierra Leonean staple
The cassava leaves must be pounded -- raw cassava leaves contain cyanide that cooking removes
Pounding breaks down the leaves and releases the cyanide
Palm oil is the essential fat for this stew
Smoked fish gives depth
Served over rice
lunch.description: Sierra Leonean cassava leaf stew -- cassava leaves (pounded to remove cyanide compounds) cooked in palm oil with smoked fish, onion, and pepper. The pounding and long cooking are essential. Served over rice.

lunch.name: Egusi Soup
instructions: Egusi soup is the West African ground melon seed soup
Egusi: the seeds of the colocynth melon -- ground into a paste
Thickens the soup naturally when cooked in palm oil
The combination of the melon seed paste with palm oil is the essential West African stew base
lunch.description: Sierra Leonean ground melon seed soup -- egusi (colocynth melon seeds) ground into a paste and cooked in palm oil with beef or smoked fish and Scotch bonnet. The egusi-palm oil combination is the West African stew base. Thick, rich, earthy.

dinner.name: Jollof Rice
instructions: Brown chicken, sauté vegetables
Add tomato paste and rice
Cook covered

dinner.name: Okra Soup
instructions: Sauté onion in palm oil
Add okra and water
Add fish and crayfish
Simmer until thick
dinner.description: Slimy okra soup with smoked fish.

dinner.name: Groundnut Soup (Peanut Soup)
ingredients: Groundnuts (peanuts -- roasted and ground into a paste)
instructions: Groundnut soup is one of the most important West African soups
The roasted peanuts give the soup its rich, nutty base
The peanut paste is cooked in palm oil with meat and tomatoes
A thick, very rich soup
Groundnut soup exists across West Africa -- from Senegal to Nigeria to Sierra Leone
dinner.description: Sierra Leonean peanut soup -- roasted groundnuts ground into a paste and cooked in palm oil with chicken or beef, tomatoes, and Scotch bonnet into a thick, rich, nutty stew. Groundnut soup spans West Africa from Senegal to Nigeria.

dinner.name: Fried Plantain
instructions: Fried plantain is eaten throughout West Africa and the Caribbean
The ripe plantain (yellow-black) is the sweetest -- best for frying
Sliced diagonally and fried until caramelized
A side dish alongside rice and stew
dinner.description: Sierra Leonean fried plantain -- ripe (yellow to black) plantain sliced diagonally and fried until caramelized. The natural sugars of the ripe plantain caramelize in the oil. A side dish alongside rice and stew throughout West Africa.

dinner.name: Okra Soup
instructions: Okra soup is a West African staple -- the okra releases its mucilage
The mucilage (the sliminess) of okra thickens the soup
Some love the thickness; some reduce it by cooking the okra with a little acid
Palm oil, smoked fish, and okra: the West African combination
dinner.description: Sierra Leonean okra soup -- sliced fresh okra cooked in palm oil with smoked fish and Scotch bonnet. The okra releases mucilage that thickens the soup. Palm oil, smoked fish, and okra: the fundamental West African combination.

snacks.name: Kuli-Kuli (Peanut Cookies)
instructions: Extract oil from peanuts
Season paste, shape
Deep fry until firm

snacks.name: Roasted Groundnuts
ingredients: Raw peanuts in shells or shelled
instructions: Roasted groundnuts are the West African roadside snack
Sold by street vendors throughout Sierra Leone
Roasted in their shells over fire or in a pan
Salty, warm, addictive
The economy of street vending: small portions sold cheaply to passersby
snacks.description: Sierra Leonean roasted groundnuts -- raw peanuts roasted in shell over fire or in a pan, salted. The ubiquitous West African street snack. Sold by vendors throughout Sierra Leone in small portions.

snacks.name: Plantain Chips
instructions: Green plantain chips are the West African crispy snack
The green, unripe plantain: starchy, not sweet
Sliced thin and fried until crispy
Salted immediately
snacks.description: Sierra Leonean green plantain chips -- unripe starchy plantain sliced thin and fried crispy, salted immediately. The West African snack staple.

snacks.name: Chin Chin
instructions: Chin chin is the West African fried dough snack
Small pieces of sweetened, spiced dough deep-fried until golden and crunchy
Shelf-stable -- lasts for weeks
Made in large quantities for celebrations
Every West African country has its chin chin tradition
snacks.description: Sierra Leonean fried dough snack -- small pieces of sweetened, nutmeg-spiced dough deep-fried until golden and crunchy. Shelf-stable and made in large quantities for celebrations. A West African celebration staple from Senegal to Nigeria.

desserts.name: Rice Pap Cake
instructions: Mix rice flour with coconut milk and sugar
Bake at 175°C 30 min

desserts.name: Puff Puff
instructions: Puff puff are the West African fried dough balls
A yeast-risen dough dropped by spoonful into hot oil
They puff up as they fry -- golden and hollow inside
Sweetened with sugar and spiced with nutmeg
The West African equivalent of a doughnut
Every country in West Africa makes puff puff
desserts.description: Sierra Leonean fried dough balls -- yeast-risen sweet, nutmeg-spiced dough dropped by spoon into hot oil until they puff up golden. The West African doughnut equivalent, eaten from Senegal to Nigeria.

desserts.name: Kanya (Peanut Brittle)
instructions: Kanya is the Sierra Leonean peanut candy
Roasted peanuts cooked in caramelized sugar
Poured out and set into a brittle
Broken into pieces
Sweet, crunchy, nutty
desserts.description: Sierra Leonean peanut brittle -- roasted peanuts cooked in caramelized sugar, poured and set into brittle, broken into pieces. Sweet, crunchy, intensely nutty. A street sweet sold throughout the country.

drinks.name: Ginger Beer
instructions: Grate ginger, boil
Strain, add sugar and lemon
Chill

drinks.name: Poyo (Palm Wine)
instructions: Tap palm tree, collect sap
Serve fresh

drinks.name: Coconut Water
instructions: Young coconut water from the coastal coconut palms
The natural electrolyte drink in tropical heat
Cracked open with a machete
Drunk fresh from the coconut
drinks.description: Sierra Leonean fresh coconut water -- young coconuts cracked open with a machete for the naturally sweet electrolyte-rich water. Available from coastal coconut palms. The natural cooling drink in tropical heat.
